findings.title: CWPdoor: The Invisible Backdoor Living Inside Control Web Panel
findings.summary_md: QiAnXin XLab disclosed cwpdoor, a passive backdoor embedded in a recompiled cwpsrv binary, the web server behind Control Web Panel versions 1.15.10 and 1.24.0. The infection script cwpsrv_update.sh was captured on June 29, 2026 and downloads the malicious binary from 136.0.141.71. A cwpsrv.suspeito sample uploaded to VirusTotal from Brazil on September 30, 2026 had zero vendor detections, which XLab cites as evidence of real victims in the wild.

findings.title: Hackers backdoor Linux servers using trojanized CWP web server
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported on November 5, 2026 that CWPdoor is distributed through a trojanized cwpsrv that replaces the legitimate binary on Control Web Panel servers. The updater script restores timestamps and wipes command history to hide the swap. XLab estimated more than 340000 CWP instances exposed on the public web, and researchers described the backdoor as exceptionally stealthy because trigger requests are suppressed from access logs.

findings.title: Hackers Hide Linux Backdoor in Control Web Panel Server to Execute Commands Without Logs
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News published on November 6, 2026 that QiAnXin XLab researchers captured the cwpsrv_update.sh installer on June 29 and that it targets cwpsrv versions 1.15.10 and 1.24.0. Attackers trigger the backdoor with signed HTTP headers and receive encrypted command output in HTTP 200 responses. The report notes the access log exclusion that removes the forensic trail of the interaction.
